title: Canonical affine coordinate-counit transpose and Tate normalization
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring killed by N>0, and S a Noetherian scheme with N invertible. Use the ordinary unbounded etale categories and Tate objects of [def-trf-section-local-comparison-data], the ordered shifted Tate coefficients, coefficient descent and compact-support comparison of [def-amb-affine-linear-trace-action], and the tower counit of [def-amb-affine-trace-construction] from the root-normalized transport [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows] and normalized Kummer projective-line data [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-data]. Define the ordered coefficient-to-Tate isomorphism recursively: at zero use the zero-shift unit; at each successor use the derived tensor of the preceding comparison and the shifted first Tate line, move the two even shifts out, apply the flat degree-zero tensor comparison and canonical pure-tensor Tate product, and add shifts. Flatness of these sheaves is the well-definedness obligation given by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. Compose coefficient descent, pullback of this isomorphism and canonical Tate pullback to identify the tower coefficient with the Tate object upstairs. Define towerAdjoint as the exceptional adjunction transpose of inverse compact-support comparison followed by the actual tower counit and the coefficient-unit comparison. Under the fixed ordered-coordinate isomorphism between the tower and standard affine d-space, define standardAdjoint from inverse Tate pullback, pullback of inverse tower-to-Tate comparison followed by towerAdjoint, and the actual exceptional base-change mate. Its Cartesian square over the identity is the second well-definedness obligation. Finally define an affine adjunction presentation to be normalized exactly when the inverse affineDualizingIso is standardAdjoint. All data are these formulas; no bare existence choice of an orientation or adjunction is made.
